cues: Mortise-and-tenon joints can keep its tall frame rigid as weight accumulates across several broad boards.
In older libraries, polished timber rows create a formal backdrop for quiet browsing and study.
A rolling ladder gives readers access to volumes placed near a room’s high ceiling.
Freestanding models may use a plinth base to prevent a narrow vertical frame from tipping.
Carved corbels beneath the upper crown add ornament without hiding the displayed literary collection.
An angled display ledge presents oversized art volumes face-out rather than packed spine-first.
